starter.material.title: The Silent Bell of Marrow's Crossing
starter.material.tagline: A one-evening adventure for newcomers, with ready-made heroes.
starter.material.description: Marrow's Crossing is a river village of forty souls whose chapel bell has rung the hour for two hundred years. Three nights ago it stopped. The sexton has not been seen since, the ferry will not run after dark, and the village council will pay twenty gold a head to whoever finds out why. You arrive at dusk, as the fog comes off the water.
starter.material.theme: A fog-bound river village, a chapel on the hill, and the crypt beneath it

playReviewUi.tour.player.welcome.title: Welcome to the table
playReviewUi.tour.player.welcome.body: This is where the adventure is played. The story runs down the middle over a painting of the scene; on a wide screen the party stands down the left, and your character, the quests and the world sit in the side panel. When a fight with a map starts, a wide screen puts the board in the middle with the story on a scroll beside it. A short tour shows the controls. Replay it any time from Help.
playReviewUi.tour.player.modes.title: How you speak
playReviewUi.tour.player.modes.body: Do describes what your character does. Say speaks in character. OOC is table talk the Dungeon Master ignores. Pick one, then write in the box below.
playReviewUi.tour.player.compose.title: Take your turn
playReviewUi.tour.player.compose.body: Type your action here and press Enter. The Dungeon Master reads everything sent up to that moment and answers the whole table at once, whether that is the AI or a person in the DM seat, so agree on a plan before you send.
playReviewUi.tour.player.battle-hand.bod: On your turn in combat your options arrive as cards: each weapon, each prepared spell, your class features and the basic actions, with the numbers from your sheet. Pick a card, pick who it lands on, then press the gold button. A dimmed card is spent; press it to hear why. Or type your move below, as ever.
playReviewUi.tour.player.talk.title: Hold to talk
playReviewUi.tour.player.talk.body: Hold the microphone and dictate instead of typing; the words land in the box for you to check before sending.
playReviewUi.tour.player.ask.title: Ask the DM
playReviewUi.tour.player.ask.body: Questions about the story, the rules or your sheet go here, not in the message box. Asking never moves the story on, so it works even while the floor is locked.
playReviewUi.tour.player.party-rail.body: Every hero's face, hit points and class, down the left of the table. A bar flashes when someone is hurt or healed, the hero whose turn it is glows, and yours is marked. Select a card to open the party.
playReviewUi.tour.player.turn-order.body: During a fight the turn order runs along the top bar, with whoever is acting lit in gold. Select a face to open the party and the full order.
playReviewUi.tour.player.party.title: The party
playReviewUi.tour.player.party.body: Everyone's hit points and conditions, and the fight order during combat. Select a card to open the full sheet: every spell, item and feature has a painted icon, and the mark beside it opens its description. The room code lives in the lead's tab.
playReviewUi.tour.player.quest.title: The quest at hand
playReviewUi.tour.player.quest.body: The party's current quest sits above the side panel so it is never out of sight. Select it to open the story, where Quests holds the whole log.
playReviewUi.tour.player.story.title: The story so far
playReviewUi.tour.player.story.body: Chapters, the facts the table has pinned, and the log of every roll and stat change the Dungeon Master made. Once a chapter closes, Open the chronicle turns the closed chapters like the pages of a book.
playReviewUi.tour.player.map.title: Maps
playReviewUi.tour.player.map.body: The scene map, the overworld and the places the party has found. While a fight with a map is running, the battle board takes the middle of a wide screen, or its own tab on a phone: the portraits along its top are the turn order, and on your turn the pips beside them show the action, bonus action and reaction you have left. Enlarge spreads the board across the whole screen, with the chronicle and a box to take your turn on its left and the turn order down its right.
playReviewUi.tour.player.stage.title: Board or story
playReviewUi.tour.player.stage.body: While a fight with a map is on, this switch picks what fills the middle of the table: the board with the chronicle beside it, or the story as usual with the board in its tab. This browser remembers your choice.
playReviewUi.tour.player.chat.title: Whispers and side chat
playReviewUi.tour.player.chat.body: Private words with the Dungeon Master, and side chat between players that never reaches the transcript.
playReviewUi.tour.player.dice.title: Dice
playReviewUi.tour.player.dice.body: Every roll is made by the server, never invented, and the latest one flashes up over the story with its total. This menu turns the tumbling 3D dice on or off, opens the editor for your own dice colours, and on a phone lets you shake to roll.
playReviewUi.tour.player.voice.title: Voice chat
playReviewUi.tour.player.voice.body: Join the call from here and talk to the table without another app. It stays up whichever panel you switch to.
playReviewUi.tour.player.help.title: Help, settings and the way home
playReviewUi.tour.player.help.body: Help explains every button. The account menu beside it holds your characters, settings, log out, and, inside the app, the way back to its home screen.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.welcome.title: You run the table
playReviewUi.tour.dm.welcome.body: You narrate in your own words; the app keeps the sheets, the dice, the maps and the record straight underneath you. This tour shows your console. Replay it any time from Help.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.modes.title: Narrate and OOC
playReviewUi.tour.dm.modes.body: Narrate writes into the story as the Dungeon Master. OOC is table talk. Player actions arrive as intents for you to answer.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.console.title: Your console
playReviewUi.tour.dm.console.body: Only the DM seats have this tab. It holds the floor, the story beats, the hand-over switches when an assistant is on, the queue of intents waiting on you, and every tool underneath.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.floor.title: Who may act
playReviewUi.tour.dm.floor.body: Open the floor to everyone or hold it while you set a scene. During a fight the initiative order holds it for you.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.beats.title: Write down what happened
playReviewUi.tour.dm.beats.body: Because you narrate out loud, jot a line or two here every so often. Beats are what chapter summaries, recaps and the exported story are built from. Draft it for me writes one from the recent play.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.delegation.title: Hand it over
playReviewUi.tour.dm.delegation.body: Let the assistant take the monsters' turn, or cover the table for a counted stretch of answers while you step away.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.queue.title: Waiting on you
playReviewUi.tour.dm.queue.body: Player actions that need a ruling gather here. What should I press? suggests the tool and fills it in.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.tools.title: Your tools
playReviewUi.tour.dm.tools.body: Assist for stat blocks, DCs and odds. Combat, Party, World, Social, Story and Table for every ruling the engine can apply. Maps, Cast, Bestiary, Storyboard and Tables for prep.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.party-rail.title: The party at a glance
playReviewUi.tour.dm.party-rail.body: Every hero's face, hit points and class, down the left of the table, the one whose turn it is glowing. Select a card to open the party.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.turn-order.title: Whose turn it is
playReviewUi.tour.dm.turn-order.body: During a fight the turn order runs along the top bar, with whoever is acting lit in gold. Select a face to open the party.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.party.title: The party
playReviewUi.tour.dm.party.body: Sheets, hit points and conditions for everyone, and during combat the initiative order you can reorder.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.map.title: Maps and the board
playReviewUi.tour.dm.map.body: The scene map and the overworld. While a fight with a map is running, the battle board takes the middle of a wide screen with the chronicle beside it, or its own tab on a phone. Enlarge spreads the board across the whole screen with the chronicle and a box to keep narrating on its left, and the turn order down its right.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.stage.title: Board or story
playReviewUi.tour.dm.stage.body: While a fight with a map is on, this switch picks what fills the middle of the table: the board with the chronicle beside it, or the story as usual with the board in its tab. This browser remembers your choice.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.chat.title: Whispers
playReviewUi.tour.dm.chat.body: Private lines to and from each player: a secret only one of them learns, or a question they did not want to ask aloud.
playReviewUi.tour.dm.help.title: Help and the way home
playReviewUi.tour.dm.help.body: Help explains every button and replays this tour. The account menu beside it holds settings, log out and, inside the app, the way back to its home screen.

entryHub.tour.welcome.title: The workshop shelf
entryHub.tour.welcome.body: A workshop is a prep space with no players and no story running: maps, people, monsters, fights, tables and rules built on your own time, then brought into a campaign when the table sits down. Each one on this shelf stands alone.
entryHub.tour.new.title: Start a workshop
entryHub.tour.new.body: Name it and say what party it is built for. Every encounter budget and odds preview inside measures against that party, so difficulty readouts mean something before real characters exist.
entryHub.tour.import.title: Import a bundle
entryHub.tour.import.body: A bundle is a whole workshop as one file, exported from the Share tool here or on another server. A world exported from WorldForge opens the same way, whole: its entries become the Cast, places, factions and lore, and the rest lands in the workshop's WorldForge tool. Importing makes a new workshop of your own; nothing is written into a campaign.
entryHub.tour.list.title: Your workshops

onboarding.title: How to play
onboarding.what: Open Dungeon Master is a Dungeons & Dragons 5e table where an AI sits in the Dungeon Master's chair, or a friend does with the AI as their assistant. You and your friends play the adventurers. The app is the rulebook and the dice.
onboarding.world: Every table runs on the 5e rules. Where it is set is up to you: a genre of your choosing, or one of the pre-built worlds your server has installed.
onboarding.create: New campaign creates the world: pick a genre, difficulty and starting level, and optionally give the DM a secret story setup only it will know. If the server has campaign plugins installed, you can pick a pre-built world here instead of a bare genre, which brings its own races, classes, monsters and lore without changing a rule. You get an eight-letter invite code to share with your friends.
onboarding.join: Solo adventure is the same thing for one player. To join someone else's table, paste their code into "Join with a room code" or open the invite link they send you.
onboarding.character: Then build a character in the creation wizard, or reuse one saved under Characters in the account menu. Everyone readies up in the lobby, and the campaign owner starts the adventure.
onboarding.rules: The app does all the calculation and gives the result to the DM, who weaves it into the story. Attack rolls, damage, saving throws, death saves, conditions, spell slots, rests, XP and level-ups are all resolved by the server against the 5e rules and written straight to your character sheet.
onboarding.log: The DM narrates what those results mean. It cannot invent a roll or quietly hand you a bonus, so play the story rather than arguing the numbers. Every roll and stat change is recorded in the Log, under the Story tab, if you want to check the maths.
onboarding.modeHint: The buttons above the message box change what your message means:
onboarding.do: Describe what your character does. The DM narrates the outcome and asks for a roll when the rules call for one.
onboarding.say: Speak in character. Your text is sent as spoken dialogue.
onboarding.ooc: Out-of-character table talk. The DM does not read it or respond to it.
onboarding.ask: To ask the DM a question about the story, the world, the rules, or your sheet, open the Ask the DM strip just above the message box. The answer quotes what the campaign has on record, and you choose whether it is just for you or for the whole table. Asking never moves the story on, so it works even while the floor is locked.
onboarding.queue: When the DM starts thinking, it reads everything sent up to that moment and writes one reply for the whole table. Anything you send while it is still thinking will not change that reply. It is picked up on the next turn, together with whatever everyone else sent.
onboarding.coordinate: So if you are playing with others, talk your options over before someone sends, then send one clear action each. Piling on more messages mid-narration does not speed the DM up or steer the reply already in progress.
onboarding.spotlight: OOC is the safe channel for that discussion: it never wakes the DM, and it still works while the floor is locked during narration. Sometimes the DM puts one player in the spotlight and waits for them, and a banner will tell you when that is why you cannot act.
onboarding.fix: Nothing the DM writes is final. Hovering one of its messages shows a row of actions. The party lead can have it reroll that moment, with the same dice and the same outcome and only the wording changed, then page between the takes and leave the best one up for the table. The lead can also have it continue a reply that stopped short, or edit the wording by hand.
onboarding.bookmark: Two of those actions are open to everyone. Anyone can check a passage against what the campaign has already established, and anyone can select a line and press the bookmark to keep that detail in front of the DM for the rest of the campaign.
onboarding.help: The Help entry, in the account menu here and in the header during a session, walks through every button and panel: the side panel tabs, the Ask strip, the per-message actions, dice options, narration voice, notes, whispers, world packs and the party lead's powers. If a spotlight leaves the table stuck, the party lead can release it.

create.noPackInfo:
A pre-built world is a coat of paint over the same 5e rules. It renames the races, classes, spells and monsters to fit its setting, tells the Dungeon Master how the place sounds, and floats the peoples and callings that belong there to the top of every picker in the character builder. Nothing is locked: you can still play a wizard in a world that calls them something else.

table.info.livingWorld.label: What does Living World do?
table.info.livingWorld.text:
On: the world moves without you. Off-screen storylines advance on background dice each turn, so rival factions, threats, and distant events keep developing while you play.

NPCs pursue their own goals between chapters and during rests and travel. Schemes progress, pressure builds, and rivals can collide with each other.

The DM quietly records what happened off-screen and weaves it into future scenes, ambushes, and rumors. These simulation notes are DM-only until the party discovers them in play.

Off: all of that pauses. The world changes only when your party acts or the story arc calls for it. Your main story arc, chapters, quests, and XP work exactly the same either way.

You can switch this at any time. Turning it back on resumes from the world as it currently stands.
table.info.bonds.label: What are Bonds?
table.info.bonds.text:
How each NPC and AI companion feels about each character, tracked by the server on one meter from hostile through neutral to devoted.

Deeds move it, and the same deed lands differently on different people: mercy wins over a kind healer and irritates a hard-bitten mercenary.

Standing shows in the Bonds tab and colors how the DM plays them. Off: the DM tracks no personal standing and NPCs react to the party as a whole.
table.info.romance.label: How does Romance work?
table.info.romance.text:
The romance ladder on top of the bond meter: interested, courting, together, betrothed, married.

Nobody can be romanced who does not already like the character, players always make the first move, and intimate scenes always fade to black.

Requires Bonds to be on.
table.info.narrationGuard.label: What is the outcome check?
table.info.narrationGuard.text:
After each turn the server compares the DM's narration against what the dice and tools actually resolved: a hit written on a miss, a death the hit points deny, a damage number no die rolled.

A contradiction is sent back to the DM once for a rewrite. Nothing on any sheet changes either way.

Off costs nothing but the check, and the narration is persisted exactly as written.

panel.title: Game settings
panel.packHint: Pick a pre-built universe to rename races, classes, spells and monsters to fit it.

panel.maxPartyLabel: Most lasting party companions allowed at once
panel.maxGuestsLabel: Most temporary guest allies allowed at once
panel.lengthTip: How far the DM plans the story ahead (acts, bosses, side quests). Changing it mid-campaign applies when the next saga is planned; any length continues with a sequel saga if you play past the finale.
panel.diceTip: Real dice lets each player opt in to rolling at their table: the game parks until they type the result, read it from a paired Pixels Bluetooth die, or let the server roll per die (Dice sources, in the Party tab).
panel.theatreTip: Theatre inserts: when a passage has someone speaking, their portrait comes up over the scene art while their lines play.
panel.ambienceTip: Pick a bed from each new place and switch to combat music when a fight starts. Off leaves every change to the DM.
panel.drawingTip: Players may draw on the live board: a plan of attack, a circle round a door. The DM always may.
panel.enemyTip: Show what enemies look likely to do next
panel.ambienceMissing: No ambience audio is installed yet, so this plays silence. Run npm run fetch-ambience on the server; setting a FREESOUND_API_KEY first widens the sources.
panel.multiclassTip: Let characters take levels in a second or third class at level-up (5e multiclassing, prerequisites enforced)
panel.joinTip: Allow new players to join with the invite code after the adventure starts
panel.heldTip: After each DM narration, players cannot act until you allow responses. OOC stays open.
panel.hpTip: How hit points grow after 1st level (1st is always the hit die's highest face plus Constitution). Rolled dice are thrown by the server.
panel.wealthTip: What a new character starts with: the class and background kit plus the background's coin, or gold the server rolls by class to buy gear with.
panel.reminderTip: How much play may pass with nothing written down before the console nudges you to record what happened. Your own typed narration counts, so a DM who writes their scenes is never nudged.
panel.rollReminderTip: The combat tempo: twelve rolls is roughly two rounds of a four-person fight.
panel.livingTip: The world moves on its own: off-screen storylines advance on background dice, surprises and encounters build up over quiet stretches, and NPC schemes progress between chapters and during rests and travel. The story arc itself is unaffected either way.
panel.livingHintOn: Rumors, surprises, and off-screen schemes advance between turns.
panel.livingHintOff: Nothing happens unless the party or the story arc makes it happen.
panel.itemsTip: When on, DM-granted loot, item removals, and gold changes become offers the owning player accepts or declines before they land on the sheet. Damage, healing and conditions have their own switch.
panel.itemsHintOn: Players confirm DM item and gold changes before they apply.
panel.itemsHintOff: DM item and gold changes apply immediately (lead can undo).
panel.vitalsTip: When on, damage, healing and conditions the AI DM or a connected agent aims at a player character wait for that player (or the lead) to confirm before they land, so a wrong target, a doubled hit or a misread rule never sticks unseen. The engine's own dice, an enemy's attack or a fall, apply as always. A slower table; off by default.
panel.vitalsHintOn: Players confirm DM damage, healing and conditions before they apply.
panel.vitalsHintOff: DM damage, healing and conditions apply immediately (lead can undo).
panel.proseTip: After each turn the server compares the DM's narration against what the dice and tools actually resolved: a hit written on a miss, a death the hit points deny, a damage number no die rolled. A contradiction is sent back to the DM once for a rewrite. Nothing on any sheet changes either way.
panel.proseHintOn: Narration that contradicts the dice goes back for one rewrite.
panel.proseHintOff: The DM's narration is persisted exactly as written.
panel.voiceTip: Live voice chat for this table, in the lobby and during play. The server also has its own switch, and needs a media port open; if voice is off server-wide this has no effect.
panel.turnTip: How hard the floor is enforced on microphones. Soft shows whose turn it is without muting anyone. Strict pauses a player's microphone on the server, so the mute is real rather than a greyed-out button. Off ignores the floor entirely. The DM is never muted by any of these.
panel.transcriptionTip: Transcription: each speaker's microphone is written down with their name, for the beat drafter and the chapter summary. Never read by the DM prompt. The lobby says out loud that the table is being transcribed while this is on.
panel.proximityTip: Distance decides who hears whom, using the battle map. Outside combat, or with no map, everyone hears everyone as usual. The DM always hears everyone and is always heard.
panel.sayRangeTip: Lets each player pick whisper (5 ft), normal, or shout (120 ft). The range is the speaker's, because shouting is something you do rather than something done to you.
panel.wallsTip: A wall between two characters muffles the voice rather than silencing it. Hearing through a door is a real thing, and audio that vanished at a doorway would read as a bug. Fog of war never gates audio: not seeing someone has nothing to do with hearing them.
panel.downedTip: A character at 0 hit points stops hearing the table. They still hear the DM, and they are still heard.
panel.bondsTip: How each NPC and AI companion feels about each character, tracked by the server on one meter from hostile through neutral to devoted. Deeds move it, and the same deed lands differently on different people: mercy wins over a kind healer and irritates a hard-bitten mercenary. Standing shows in the Bonds tab and colors how the DM plays them.
panel.romanceTip: The romance ladder on top of the bond meter: interested, courting, together, betrothed, married. Nobody can be romanced who does not already like the character, players always make the first move, and intimate scenes always fade to black.
panel.bondsHintOff: The DM tracks no personal standing; NPCs react to the party as a whole.
panel.romanceHintOn: Standing is tracked per character, and romance can grow from it.
panel.romanceHintOff: Standing is tracked per character; romance is off.
panel.companionsTip: AI companions the DM plays: 'party members' travel with the party until dismissed; 'guests' are temporary allies for one scene or battle (a town soldier helping defend) and leave automatically when the fight ends. Auto picks full for solo play, guests only for multiplayer.
